subject: Culture
title: Honor in the American South
description: One-minute skill: Honor in the American South.

hook.text: Psychologists insulted students in a hallway. Southerners' cortisol spiked. Northerners shrugged.

buildup.text: Richard Nisbett traced southern honor culture to Scots-Irish herders who settled the backcountry.

discovery.text: Herders had no fences or police. Projecting toughness was the only way to protect livestock.

twist.text: Centuries later, those counties still have higher argument-based homicide rates than farming regions.

climax.text: Culture of honor explains why 'stand your ground' laws passed easily in former herding states.

punchline.text: Herding vanished. The reflexes it built did not.

quiz.question: Who linked southern US honor culture to herding ancestry?

details.summary: The American South developed a distinct honor culture shaped by Scots-Irish settlers, plantation aristocracy, and frontier violence. Southern honor demanded aggressive defense of reputation, chivalric protection of women, and willingness to duel.
details.whyItMatters: Southern honor culture explains persistent regional differences in violence, gun culture, military enlistment, and social norms in the United States — differences often misattributed to race or economics alone.
takeaways: Nisbett and Cohen proved Southern men respond more aggressively to insults
Southern honor has Scots-Irish herding culture origins
Dueling persisted longer in the South than any other US region

faq.question: What did Nisbett and Cohen's research show?
faq.answer: In controlled experiments, University of Michigan researchers insulted Southern and Northern college students (being bumped and called a derogatory name).

faq.question: Where did Southern honor culture come from?
faq.answer: Scots-Irish settlers brought herding-culture honor norms (protecting livestock required fearsome reputation). Plantation culture added aristocratic honor elements (dueling, chivalry, gentlemanly conduct). Frontier conditions with weak law enforcement reinforced self-reliance and personal violence.
